reason: Regular people in this passage are predominantly portrayed unfavorably or neutrally. The Egyptian magicians and wise men (חרטמי מצרים וחכמיה) are shown as incompetent, unable to interpret Pharaoh's dreams despite being summoned. The Egyptian populace is depicted as desperate and suffering—crying out to Pharaoh for bread during the famine (וַיִּצְעַ֥ק הָעָ֛ם). While the chief cupbearer is somewhat helpful in remembering Joseph, he is also portrayed as forgetful for two years. The passage elevates Joseph as divinely exceptional, implicitly contrasting God's wisdom with the inadequacy of ordinary Egyptian power and knowledge. Regular people are presented as either ineffectual or as victims of circumstance, not favorably.
